title: The naming
hook: a name chosen, a name changed, and a man who refused to change his

segments.voice: Yesterday, tahnik, and your line: sweetness first. Did someone get something sweet from you before anything else? In both of yesterday's stories, the date came with a name. Today, the name. Day one thousand three hundred twenty.

Rough ground. Hard, rugged ground. That's what the name Hazn means, and a man who carried it comes to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. The Prophet asks his name, hears it, and offers him another: Sahl, easy, smooth ground. Hazn says no. I won't change a name my father gave me. His grandson tells this story in Sahih al-Bukhari, and adds a quiet line of his own: that roughness stayed in the family afterward. A name, in this story, is not just a label. Today: the naming.
screen: `HAZN: ROUGH GROUND.` → `OFFERED SAHL: EASY GROUND.` → `HE KEEPS HIS FATHER'S NAME.`

segments.voice: First, names go back to the beginning. In surah al-Baqarah, in Pickthall's translation: "And He taught Adam all the names." In the Qur'an, the names are what Allah teaches Adam. Second, when. Some reports have the Prophet naming a baby the day it was brought to him: Abu Musa's son Ibrahim, Umm Sulaym's son 'Abdullah, both from yesterday. Another report, in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi, mentions naming on the seventh day, along with other things done that day that belong to the coming lessons. So families name on the first day, or the seventh, and both have a basis. Third, what makes a name good. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says, in paraphrase: the most beloved of your names to Allah are 'Abdullah and 'Abd al-Rahman. Servant of Allah. Servant of the Most Merciful. A name that says whose the child is. Fourth, names can be changed. Also in Muslim, Ibn 'Umar reports that a daughter of 'Umar was named 'Asiyah, which sounds like disobedient, and the Prophet renamed her Jamilah: beautiful. That's the background to Hazn's story. More than once, the Prophet lifted a heavy name into a lighter one, and Hazn chose to keep his. Put together, the picture is simple. A name is one of the earliest gifts a child is handed, and one they'll hear again and again for the rest of their life. Every time someone calls them, the meaning gets said out loud.
screen: `HE TAUGHT ADAM ALL THE NAMES.` · `THE FIRST DAY, OR THE SEVENTH.` · `'ABDULLAH, 'ABD AL-RAHMAN.` · `'ASIYAH BECOMES JAMILAH.`

segments.voice: The practice: learn what your name means. Not online yet; first, settle, and breathe. Say your own name silently, slowly, the way someone who loves you says it. Who chose it? Was it for a grandparent, a saint, a sound someone liked, a hope? If you don't know, notice that too. Then hold the question: if your name were a meaning said out loud every time you're called, what would you want it to say? After the bell, look up what it means. If you pray, you can make du'a for whoever named you. The bell holds the time.
The naming. A good name given on the first day or the seventh, beloved when it says whose the child is, and changed when the meaning is heavy. Today's word.

Your line: a good name. Today, find out what your name means, and use someone else's name kindly and correctly at least once. Tomorrow, the seventh-day sacrifice. Day one thousand three hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Muslim parents choose a name with a good meaning for a newborn, on the day of birth or on the seventh day, and names such as 'Abdullah and 'Abd al-Rahman are favored after the hadith in Sahih Muslim.
